newsitem.title: USA: NFL-TRADE DEADLINE PASSES WITH JEFF GEORGE STILL IN ATLANTA. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT 9/10/96]
newsitem.headline: NFL-TRADE DEADLINE PASSES WITH JEFF GEORGE STILL IN ATLANTA. [CORRECTED 01:15 GMT 9/10/96]

text.p: The NFL trading deadline came and went Tuesday, leaving quarterback Jeff George still a disgruntled, suspended member of the Atlanta Falcons.

Both the Falcons and the Seattle Seahawks -- where George was rumoured to be headed in a trade for quarterback Rick Mirer -- announced shortly after the afternoon deadline that no deal had been reached.

A Seahawks spokesman said Monday that George, who can become a free agent at the end of the season, was offered a multi-year deal by the team which ESPN reported to be $30 million over six years (Corrects from five years.)
Apparently, George never agreed to the contract and the proposed deal fell through.
No other trades were immediately announced. Because of salary cap restrictions, there usually is very little action before the deadline.

The Oakland Raiders also were reported to be interested in George, offering quarterback Jeff Hostetler and defensive end Chester McGlockton to the Falcons. Raiders coach Mike White denied the report on Monday.

George remains a member of the winless Falcons, who suspended him for four weeks after television cameras caught his heated argument with coach June Jones on the sidelines during a September 22 home game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The argument came after George threw his second interception of the game in the third quarter and Jones replaced him with Bobby Hebert. The following day, George was suspended for "conduct detrimental to the team."
Hebert is winless in two starts for Atlanta (0-5), which made the playoffs last season.

George was a transition free agent after the 1995 season and held out of training camp for 24 days before agreeing on a one-year contract worth $3.363 million on August 6. It was the highest year's pay in team history, but George was unhappy about not receiving a multi-year pact.
Mirer, the second overall pick in the 1993 draft, was benched Sunday after a poor start this season. John Friesz replaced him and threw three long touchdown passes in a 22-15 victory at Miami.
